links.effect: Sensitivity 0.957 (95% CI 0.939-0.971) internal vs 0.943 (0.921-0.961) external; external AI exceeded clinicians' 0.658.
links.quote: The AI model in the internal dataset achieved a patient-level diagnostic sensitivity of 0·957 (95% CI 0·939-0·971) and a higher patient-level diagnostic sensitivity than clinicians (0·943 [0·921-0·961] vs 0·658 [0·644-0·672]; p<0·0001) in the external dataset.

models_evaluated: CTA-based deep-learning model for intracranial aneurysm detection

links.outcome: Model errors associated with poor-quality clinical images and recognition failure
links.effect: The prospective error rate was 0·51% (8/1570), attributed to poor-quality CTA images and recognition failure.
links.quote: In the prospective study, the AI model had a 0·51% (8/1570) error rate due to poor-quality CTA images and recognition failure.

links.outcome: AI versus clinician patient-level diagnostic sensitivity on external validation cases
links.effect: External patient-level sensitivity was 0·943 [0·921-0·961] for AI vs 0·658 [0·644-0·672] for clinicians; p<0·0001.
links.quote: The AI model in the internal dataset achieved a patient-level diagnostic sensitivity of 0·957 (95% CI 0·939-0·971) and a higher patient-level diagnostic sensitivity than clinicians (0·943 [0·921-0·961] vs 0·658 [0·644-0·672]; p<0·0001) in the external dataset.

links.outcome: Clinician diagnostic AUC and sensitivity with versus without AI in prospective clinical use
links.quote: The model had a high negative predictive value of 0·998 (0·994-1·000) and significantly improved the diagnostic performance of clinicians; AUC improved from 0·787 (95% CI 0·766-0·808) to 0·909 (0·894-0·923; p<0·0001) and patient-level sensitivity improved from 0·590 (0·511-0·666) to 0·825 (0·759-0·880; p<0·0001).

links.effect: AI-assisted strategy improved clinicians' diagnostic AUC from 0.795 to 0.878 on a per-patient basis.
links.quote: In the multi-reader multi-case study, the AI-assisted strategy improved clinicians' diagnostic performance both on a per-patient basis (the area under the receiver operating characteristic curves [AUCs]; 0·795 [0·761-0·830] without AI vs 0·878 [0·850-0·906] with AI; p<0·0001) and a per-aneurysm basis (the area under the weighted alternative free-response receiver operating characteristic curves; 0·765 [0·732-0·799] vs 0·865 [0·839-0·891]; p<0·0001).

links.effect: AI model achieved a higher patient-level diagnostic sensitivity than clinicians alone (0.943 vs 0.658).
links.quote: The AI model in the internal dataset achieved a patient-level diagnostic sensitivity of 0·957 (95% CI 0·939-0·971) and a higher patient-level diagnostic sensitivity than clinicians (0·943 [0·921-0·961] vs 0·658 [0·644-0·672]; p<0·0001) in the external dataset.

links.effect: In prospective deployment, AI significantly improved clinician AUC from 0.787 to 0.909 and sensitivity from 0.590 to 0.825.
links.quote: The model had a high negative predictive value of 0·998 (0·994-1·000) and significantly improved the diagnostic performance of clinicians; AUC improved from 0·787 (95% CI 0·766-0·808) to 0·909 (0·894-0·923; p<0·0001) and patient-level sensitivity improved from 0·590 (0·511-0·666) to 0·825 (0·759-0·880; p<0·0001).

links.effect: Clinicians in the AI-assisted group demonstrated high acceptance with a 92.6% adoption rate.
links.quote: In the randomised open-label comparison study, clinicians in the AI-assisted group had a high acceptance of the AI model (92·6% adoption rate), and a higher AUC when compared with the control group (0·858 [95% CI 0·850-0·866] vs 0·789 [0·780-0·799]; p<0·0001).
